newsitem.title: USA: American Brands to take $80 million charge.
newsitem.headline: American Brands to take $80 million charge.

text.p: American Brands Inc. said Thursday it will take about $80 million in charges in the fourth quarter to consolidate operations and cut 950 jobs at its British-based Gallaher tobacco unit.

The international consumer products holding company said steps being reviewed to raise productivity at its remaining operations may result in more restructuring charges before it spins off Gallagher to shareholders. The spinoff was announced in October.
Gallagher will consolidate cigarette making at its factory at Lisnafillan, Northern Ireland, and close its factory in Manchester, England, over the next three to four years, the company said.
The closure of the Hyde factory will result in the elimination of about 950 positions, partly offset by the creation of about 300 new jobs in Lisnafillan, it said.
Gallaher has already reduced its work force by 37 percent over the past six years.

Gallaher plans to invest 40 million pounds ($66.4 million) over the next three to four years in expanding the Lisnafillan factory and installing the latest generation of ultra-high speed cigarette manufacturing machinery.
American Brands said the charges, which equal about $55 million after tax, mainly cover employee termination benefits.

"Gallaher is the U.K. tobacco market leader and has a significant and growing presence in continental Europe," said Thomas C. Hays, American Brands' chairman and chief executive. "The plan will result in substantially lower costs for Gallaher, enhancing its competitive position and strategic flexibility."

American Brands, based in Old Greenwich, Conn., in October announced plans to spin off Gallaher to stockholders. The transaction is expected to be completed in the second or early in the third quarter of 1997, subject to favourable tax rulings and relevant stockholder approvals.
When the spin-off is completed, American Brands will be renamed Fortune Brands.
"We are firmly committed to reducing our overall cost structure, not only at Gallaher, but also at the operations that will comprise Fortune Brands," Hays said.
Excluding the $80 million restructuring charge, American Brands said it still expects to achieve its previously announced target of increasing earnings per share by 10 percent in 1996.

In December 1994, American Brands sold The American Tobacco Co. In 1995, it sold Franklin Life and several nonstrategic businesses and product lines, including its British retailing operations. Early this year, it acquired Cobra Golf, substantially enhancing its global leadership in the fast-growing golf business.
American Brands has also invested $1.8 billion during 1995 and 1996 to reduce fully diluted shares by 20 percent, and invested over $400 million in capital projects.
American Brands' stock rose 12.5 cents to $48.375 on the New York Stock Exchange at mid-morning.
